gate_rationale: Strict bug fix, no flag. The alignment width is declared by the processor cspec (<funcptr align="N"/>), not by kuna; upstream Ghidra honours it unconditionally; the rule body was already a line-for-line port whose only input was a hard-coded 0 stub; and the pre-fix C stated a bit-clear the program never performs. Both parity gates stay green with the fix live, with no re-pin and no per-test opt-out. Recorded in docs/history.md under Convergences (upstream behavior restored), which is where the registry puts a port defect whose fix moves kuna back onto upstream's default.
decisions: No option gate. CLAUDE.md carves out 'a strict bug fix that only corrects wrong output needs no flag'; this finishes a stubbed port (funcptr_align() returned a hard-coded 0), the width comes from the vendored cspec rather than from kuna, and the ablation is 0/675 with no re-pin.

Honour align=4 on AARCH64 exactly as align=2 on ARM. Upstream RuleFuncPtrEncoding::applyOp has a single code path (slide = ~0 << align) with no align special-case, and the comparison is exact, so a `& ~3` matches on AARCH64 and a `& ~1` does not. Confirmed empirically against stock Ghidra 12.1 headless on a purpose-built AArch64 probe: Ghidra strips the program's own `and x8, x8, #0xfffffffffffffffc` before `blr x8` and prints (**(code **)(param_1 + 2))(*param_1), byte-for-byte what kuna now prints.

AArch64's own lifting emits no mask (AARCH64base.sinc:887 `:blr Rn_GPR64 { pc = Rn_GPR64; ... call [pc]; }`), so the rule is inert on ordinary AArch64 code and only fires on a mask the program itself wrote.

No interaction with thumbfuncptr (GH-8471 / DIV-2), the other live funcptr_align reader: this rule only removes an INT_AND that a CALLIND consumes, and rewrites it to a transparent COPY, so any other reader keeps the value. Pinned by pass 2 of the stage test and by the unchanged gh8471-thumbfuncptr.xml.

why_ship_without_a_ged_win: The win is correctness and readability, and it is measured directly instead: kuna's post-fix C is byte-for-byte Ghidra's on both the ARM witness and the AArch64 probe, the invented bit-clear is gone (masks 264 -> 15 on cf2.elf, 459 -> 40 on nuttx), and the callee type is finally recovered (`(code **)` 0 -> 205 and 0 -> 397 on those two, where every ARM project in the corpus previously had zero).
